title: Redesign collapsed tab tiles for better readability
summary: When the sidebar is collapsed to its narrow strip, each open tab used to show as a small square box with an uppercase label and, for shared sessions, a tiny "Shared" tag. Now each tab is a wider, shorter row with a slightly larger passage name, a soft gray highlight on the selected tab, smaller participant dots for shared sessions, and a thin divider line above the list. The "Shared" tag is gone; shared sessions are now recognized by their participant dots.

setup.title: Open the preview on a computer
setup.body: Use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop, with the browser window at full width. Open the preview link above. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page still looks like the old Seed Bible, do a hard refresh (**Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac).

setup.title: Open a few tabs
setup.body: In the tab list on the left, use the add-tab button (**+**) to open three tabs, and set them to **John 3**, **Psalm 139** and **1 Thessalonians 5**. These are used in the tests below.

setup.title: Collapse the sidebar
setup.body: At the top left of the sidebar, click the menu button (its tooltip says **Collapse sidebar**). The sidebar shrinks to a narrow strip down the left edge, and your tabs show as a short list inside it. This narrow strip is what every test below looks at. Clicking the same button again (tooltip **Expand sidebar**) opens it back up.

sections.title: The new tab list in the collapsed sidebar

tests.title: Each tab shows as a full-width row with a readable passage name
tests.why: This is the main change: tabs used to be small square boxes with tiny labels.
steps: Look at the list of tabs in the collapsed sidebar.
expected: Each tab is a row that fills the width of the narrow strip (not a small square box).
Each row shows its passage name as a short book code and chapter, for example `JHN 3` or `PSA 139`, in slightly larger text than before.
The names fit on one line and aren't cut off at the edges of the strip.
There's a thin horizontal line above the first tab, separating the list from the buttons above it.
Below the last tab there's a **+** button the same width as the tabs, with no box around it.

tests.title: The selected tab is highlighted in gray and its name is bold
steps: Click the **John 3** tab in the collapsed sidebar.
Click the **Psalm 139** tab.
expected: The reader switches to the chapter you clicked each time.
The tab you clicked last has a soft gray background and a bold, darker name.
The other tabs have no background and a lighter, non-bold name.
Only one tab is highlighted at a time.

tests.title: Hovering a tab shows a faint highlight
steps: Move the mouse over a tab that isn't selected, without clicking.
Move the mouse over the selected tab.
Move the mouse over the **+** button.
expected: The unselected tab gets a very faint gray background while the mouse is over it, and loses it when the mouse leaves.
The selected tab keeps the same gray highlight (it doesn't flicker or change).
The **+** button also gets a faint gray background on hover.
Hovering a tab shows its passage name as a tooltip.

tests.title: The add button still opens a new tab
steps: Click the **+** button below the tabs in the collapsed sidebar.
expected: A new tab appears in the list as a row like the others, and it becomes the selected (gray) tab.
The sidebar stays collapsed.

tests.title: Many tabs scroll without breaking the layout
steps: Click **+** until you have about 15 tabs.
Scroll the tab list in the collapsed sidebar up and down (mouse wheel or trackpad).
expected: The tabs stay as evenly spaced rows and don't overlap.
The list scrolls, and the thin divider line and the **+** button scroll with it.
You can still reach and click every tab.

tests.title: A long book name still fits in its row
tests.why: Names are in larger text now, and the selected one is bold. The code keeps names on one line, so a name that doesn't fit could spill over the edge.
steps: Select the **1 Thessalonians 5** tab.
Also open tabs for **Psalm 119** and **Lamentations 3**, select each one so its name turns bold, and look at those rows.
expected: Each name fits inside the narrow strip, with nothing cut off or running past the strip's edges.
If a name does spill over or get cut off, mark this test **Fail** and note which book.

tests.title: A tab playing audio shows a small speaker under its name
steps: Select the **John 3** tab.
Start audio with the **Play** button in the reader's toolbar.
While it plays, select a different tab in the collapsed sidebar, then look at the John 3 row.
expected: The John 3 row shows a small speaker icon below its passage name, in the app's accent color.
The speaker icon is there whether or not John 3 is the selected tab.
When you pause the audio, the speaker icon goes away.

tests.title: A shared session tab shows participant dots and no "Shared" tag
tests.why: The tiny "Shared" tag that used to sit at the top of shared-session tabs was removed on purpose; the participant dots now mark a shared session.
tests.before: Signing in is needed to start a session. Sign in with your email (Seed Bible emails you a code). Use a second browser, or a private/incognito window (Ctrl+Shift+N in Chrome/Edge, Ctrl+Shift+P in Firefox; Cmd instead of Ctrl on Mac), as the guest.
steps: Expand the sidebar, open **Luke 2** in a tab, click **Share**, then **Start and share session**. A link is copied to your clipboard.
Paste the link into the second browser or private window and open it.
Back in the first browser, collapse the sidebar again and look at the session's tab.
expected: The session tab's row shows its passage name with small colored dots below it, one per person in the session (up to three, then a `+` number).
Your dot as the host has a thin orange ring around it.
There is no "Shared" label on the tab.
The row is the same height as the other tabs, or only slightly taller, and nothing overlaps.

tests.title: The tab list reads well in dark mode
tests.why: The highlight color now comes from the text color instead of the theme's tab colors, so it should look like a neutral gray in both themes.
steps: Switch Seed Bible to the dark theme in its settings.
Collapse the sidebar if it opened, and look at the tab list.
Click a couple of tabs and hover over others.
expected: The selected tab has a soft light-gray highlight on the dark background, and its name is bold and clearly readable.
Unselected tab names are dimmer but still readable.
The divider line above the list is visible.
Hover highlights are faint but visible.

tests.title: Things that should not have changed: the expanded sidebar
steps: Expand the sidebar with the menu button (tooltip **Expand sidebar**).
Look at the tab list, and click between tabs.
expected: The expanded sidebar's tab list looks and works the same as on the main Seed Bible site; only the collapsed list changed.

tests.title: Things that should not have changed: phone width
steps: Make the browser window very narrow (about the width of a phone), or open the preview on a phone.
Open the tab list from the app's menu.
expected: The tab list opens as the full menu, as before, not the narrow collapsed strip.

notCovered: The co-host ring color on participant dots, which needs a session with a co-host assigned; it uses the same styling as the host ring checked above.
Screen reader labels for the tabs, which this change didn't touch.
